rows.subtopic: Sum of n Terms of an AP
rows.text:
The **fourth** and **seventh** terms of an Arithmetic Progression **(A.P.)**, are **60** and **114** respectively. Find the:
(a) first term and common difference.
(b) sum of its first 10 terms.

Given, \(A = \begin{bmatrix} 3 & 1 \\ 5 & 3 \end{bmatrix}\) and \(B = \begin{bmatrix} -1 & a \\ 3 & -5 \end{bmatrix}\) and product \(AB = \begin{bmatrix} b & 7 \\ 4 & 5 \end{bmatrix}\).
Find the values of '\(a\)' and '\(b\)'.
In the given diagram, O is the centre of the circle and the tangent DE touches the circle at B. If, \(\angle ADB = 32^\circ\). Find the values of \(x\) and \(y\).

figure.note: Circle centre O; diameter CA drawn horizontally (C left, A right) and produced to D on the left; tangent from D touches the circle at B and continues to E. Chords BC and BA drawn. Angle ADB at D marked 32°; x marked at A (angle BAC); y marked at B between the tangent BE and chord BA (angle EBA).

rows.text:
The polynomial \(kx^3 + 3x^2 - 11x - 6\) when divided by \((x + 1)\), leaves a remainder of **6**.
(a) Find the value of \(k\).
(b) Using the value of \(k\) factorise completely the polynomial \(kx^3 + 3x^2 - 11x - 6\)

An eye drop bottle is prepared consisting of a hemisphere, a cylinder and a conical **cap**, as shown in the given diagram. **Height** of the cylindrical and conical parts are each, **equal to the diameter (7 cm)**. Find the:
(a) minimum height of the cylindrical box required to pack this bottle.
(b) volume of the liquid medicine (shaded part) in the bottle. Give your answer to the nearest whole number. **(Use \(\pi = \frac{22}{7}\))**

figure.note: A cone (cap) sits on top of a cylinder; a dashed vertical axis runs through both. Inside the cylinder a hemispherical arc rises from the base. The cylinder is shaded light grey (the liquid). Base diameter labelled 7 cm.

rows._flag: Check on the crop whether the shading covers the region under the hemispherical dome or only the cylinder outside it: part (b) depends on it.

rows.text:
Use ruler and compass for the following construction:
(a) construct an **equilateral** triangle ABC of side 5 cm.
(b) construct the **circumcircle** of \(\Delta ABC\).
(c) construct the locus of points which are **equidistant** from AB and BC. Mark the point where the circumcircle and locus meet, as D.
(d) give the **geometrical** name of quadrilateral ABCD.

Prove that:
\((\sec\theta - \cos\theta)(\operatorname{cosec}\theta - \sin\theta) = \sin\theta\cos\theta\)

rows.subtopic: GST with Discount and Inverse Cases
rows.text:
The cost price of a TV set is **₹ 20,000**. The shopkeeper marked it for **₹ 24,000**. He sells it to a customer at a **discount of 10%** on the marked price. If the sale is intra-state and the rate of **GST** is 12%, find the:
(a) discounted price of the TV set.
(b) amount paid by the customer to clear the bill.

In the given diagram, \(DE \parallel BC\) and \(AD : DB = 2 : 3\).
(a) Prove that: \(\Delta ADE \sim \Delta ABC\) and hence find \(DE : BC\)
(b) Prove: \(\Delta DFE \sim \Delta CFB\)
(c) Given, area of \(\Delta DFE = 16\) square units, find the **area of \(\Delta CFB\).**

figure.note: Triangle ABC (A top, B bottom left, C bottom right); D on AB and E on AC with DE parallel to BC (arrow marks on DE and BC); DC and EB drawn, intersecting at F.

rows.text:
The histogram drawn on the graph represents the number of students of different heights (in cm).
Using the graph, answer the following:
(a) the number of students whose height is **150 cm** and above.
(b) the modal height.
(c) the total number of students.

figure.note: Histogram on graph paper. Scale: x-axis, 2 cm = 10 cm of height; y-axis, 2 cm = 2 students. x-axis 'Height (cm)' marked 100 to 170 in steps of 10 (kink at origin); y-axis 'Number of Students' marked 0 to 16 in steps of 2. Bars: 100-110 height 6, 110-120 height 2, 120-130 height 9, 130-140 height 14, 140-150 height 12, 150-160 height 9, 160-170 height 4. The mode construction is already drawn inside the 130-140 bar (two crossing lines from the tops of the neighbouring bars, and a vertical line from their intersection to the x-axis, between 130 and 140).

(a) ratio in which 'P' divides AB.
(b) coordinates of point P.

Solve the quadratic equation \((x - 2)^2 - 5x - 3 = 0\) and give your answer correct to 3 significant figures.
*(Use Mathematical Tables for this question if necessary.)*

Kabir bought 120 shares of a company with nominal value ₹ 100, available at a **premium** of ₹ 25. Find:
(a) the money invested by Kabir in buying these shares.
(b) the rate of dividend, if he received ₹ 1,080 as dividend from these shares after one year.
(c) his rate of return.

**Take assumed mean = 28**

| Class Interval | 0 – 8 | 8 – 16 | 16 – 24 | 24 – 32 | 32 – 40 | 40 – 48 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Frequency | 10 | 20 | 14 | 16 | 18 | 22 |
The **difference** of two natural numbers is **5** and sum of their reciprocals is \(\frac{3}{10}\). Find the two numbers.

A flagpole is erected at the top of a building. The angle of elevation of the top and foot of the flagpole from a point **100 m** away, on the same level as that of the foot of the building, are \(33^\circ\) and \(31^\circ\) respectively. Find the height of the flagpole. Give your answer correct to the nearest metre.
*(Use Mathematical Tables for this question.)*

figure.note: Right triangle: A on the ground, B the foot of the building, AB = 100 m; BC the building, CD the flagpole with a flag at D. Lines AC and AD drawn; angle CAB marked 31°, angle DAB marked 33°. The box's top-left corner may take in the ends of two text lines; crop by hand.

rows.text:
Using a graph paper, draw an ogive for the following distribution which shows a record of weight in kilograms of **100** students.

| Weight (in kg) | Number of students |
|---|---|
| 35 – 40 | 4 |
| 40 – 45 | 6 |
| 45 – 50 | 10 |
| 50 – 55 | 24 |
| 55 – 60 | 26 |
| 60 – 65 | 17 |
| 65 – 70 | 8 |
| 70 – 75 | 5 |

Use your ogive to estimate the following:
(a) the median weight of the students.
(b) percentage of students whose weight is 60 kg or more.
(c) the weight above which 20% of the students lie.

Rohit and Vinay both opened a recurring deposit account in a bank for 2 years at 8% simple interest. Vinay deposited ₹ 300 per month. On maturity, Rohit's interest was ₹ 800 **more** than Vinay's interest. Find the:
(a) interest earned by Vinay.
(b) sum deposited by Rohit every month.

The **fourth** term of a Geometric Progression **(G.P.)** is 16 and its **seventh** term is 128. Find its:
(a) common ratio
(b) first term

rows.subtopic: Reflection in the Axes and the Origin
rows.text:
Use graph sheet for this question. Take **2 cm = 1 unit** along both \(x\) and \(y\) axis. Graphically represent parallelogram **OABC**, where O(0, 0), A(2, 3), B(5, 3) and C(3, 0).
Reflect OABC:
(a) on the \(x\)-axis and name its image as ODEC.
(b) through the origin and name its image as OIJH.
(c) on the \(y\)-axis and name its image as OFGH.

rows.subtopic: Solution Sets on the Number Line
rows.text:
Solve the following inequation, write the **solution set** and represent it on the **real number line**.
\(-1 < \frac{2x - 3}{3} - \frac{x}{5} \le 1, x \in \mathbf{R}\)

Use the following graph and answer the given questions:
(a) Write the co-ordinates of points **A**, **B** and **C**.
(b) Find the equation of a line passing through the **mid-point** of **AC** and parallel to **AB**.

figure.note: Graph paper with axes x'x and y'y; x marked -2 to 6, y marked -1 to 8, one unit per labelled division. Triangle ABC drawn with its vertices on grid points: A at the top, B at the left end and C at the right end of a horizontal side BC.

rows.text:
A solid wooden toy is prepared by joining a cone, a cylinder and a sphere, as shown in the given diagram. **The radius of each of the three solids is 7 cm** and **heights** of each of the cone and the cylinder is **24 cm**. Find:
(a) the **total surface area** of the given solid.
(b) the **cost** of painting the total surface at the rate of **₹ 0.50** per \(\text{cm}^2\).
**(Use \(\pi = \frac{22}{7}\))**

figure.note: Vertical stack on a dashed axis: a sphere (radius 7 cm) on top, a cylinder (radius 7 cm, height 24 cm) in the middle, a cone (base radius 7 cm, height 24 cm) at the bottom. Labels: 7 cm (sphere radius), 7 cm (cylinder top radius), 24 cm, 7 cm (cylinder bottom radius), 24 cm, 7 cm (cone base radius).

rows._flag: As drawn, the sphere overlaps the cylinder's top face and the cone's APEX (not its base) touches the centre of the cylinder's bottom face, with the cone's base at the very bottom. Transcribed as printed; the intended way the solids are joined (and so the TSA) should be checked against the figure.

rows.subtopic: Componendo and Dividendo and Other Properties
rows.text:
If \(x = \frac{5ab}{a - b}, a \ne b\),
(a) Find: \(\frac{x}{a}\)
(b) Using properties of proportion, find: \(\frac{x + a}{x - a}\)

A survey was conducted on **300** families having **2** children each. The results obtained are given below.

| Number of girl child | 2 | 1 | 0 | Total |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Number of families | 95 | 165 | 40 | 300 |

If one family is selected at random, find the probability that it will have:
(a) one girl child
(b) one or more girl child
(c) no boy child
In the given figure 'O' is the centre of the circle. PQ is a tangent to the circle at B and **AB = AC**. If \(\angle CBQ = 40^\circ\), find the unknown angles \(x, y, z\) and \(w\).

Chords AB and AC carry equal tick marks; chords AE, AD, DC and BC drawn; a line from B through O to E; OC drawn. x marked at A between AB and AC; z at D between DA and DC; y at O between OB and OC; w at B between BA and BO.
